source.title: DNN or k-NN: That is the Generalize vs. Memorize Question
source.authors: Gilad Cohen; G. Sapiro; R. Giryes

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper conceptually tests whether memorization and generalization coexist, using classifier agreement and layerwise behavior rather than a direct reproduction of Zhang et al.'s experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on natural labels, randomized labels, and induced overfitting. Its comparisons to prior work on batch size and memorization are cited background, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own natural-label generalization and perfect random-label training fit for Wide-Resnet on MNIST and CIFAR-10/100, extending V1 to another architecture. Its main classifier-agreement measures address a separate question.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion. They argue that memorization and generalization are compatible and complementary, and interpret near-total prediction agreement as evidence that deep networks approximate nearest-neighbor decisions in learned embeddings. Matching train/test k-NN-to-DNN KL trends accompanies generalization; separation accompanies overfitting. These observations support their interpretation rather than establishing that nearest-neighbor behavior causes generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares DNN predictions with k-NN, SVM, and LR fitted to learned representations; it does not reproduce the original random-label generalization experiments directly.
record.method_sensitivity: The train/test KL correspondence changes after memorization; under overfitting it lessens for MNIST and CIFAR-10, and occurs slightly before memorization for CIFAR-100.

fits_no_version.finding: Classifiers fitted to learned representations match DNN test accuracy and increasingly agree with its predictions; deep-network k-NN agreement approaches 100%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DNN predictions closely resemble nearest-neighbor classification in their learned embedding spaces.

fits_no_version.finding: Train/test k-NN-to-DNN KL trends separate during random-label memorization or induced overfitting; SVM/LR separation is inconsistent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Separation of training and testing k-NN-to-DNN KL trends can indicate overfitting.

record.problems: Several relevant results are presented only in figures without numerical values. The text does not state random-label test accuracy or directly report chance-level accuracy. The CIFAR-100 overfitting result is described as data not shown.

untested.parts: Chance-level random-label held-out accuracy is not established quantitatively. Identical training recipes across natural and randomized labels, and the absence of explicit regularization in that comparison, are not documented.
No width sweep across the interpolation threshold.
The supplied prose gives no convolutional-versus-fully-connected test-error ordering or controlled test of local connectivity; architecture-specific Figure 1 values are unavailable.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or rankings of generalization measures.
No removal of examples selected by label memorization and comparison with random removal.

missing.what: Direct randomized-label DNN training accuracy reaches 100%; add dataset-specific accuracy rows rather than recording only KL divergence or layerwise probe accuracy.

Direct natural-label Wide-Resnet training and test accuracy trajectories appear in Figure 5's top row. Their numerical levels are unavailable in the supplied text and should be extracted from the figure.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for the listed versions. Figure plots are absent from the supplied text, so numerical accuracy levels cannot be reconstructed. Its use of memorization as nearest-neighbor storage also differs from V1's operational definition of fitting random labels.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not establish that the same training recipe achieves both near-perfect random-label fit and far-above-chance natural-label test performance, or report numerical natural-label and random-label test accuracies in the text.
Magnitude-aware perturbations and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures are not tested.
